newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pare gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pare gains at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks snapped a negative streak Tuesday but lost momentum towards the close and were seen hesitant near-term, dealers said.
"Trading was very erratic today. We had a good start but then a bout of speculative profit-taking which knocked down Wall Street," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index slipped off a high of 730 to end at 721 with a gain of 0.6 percent. It had shed 3.3 percent in the previous five consecutive sessions of losses.
"The market will now try to find a floor which should not be less than yesterday's intra-day low of 703," Bonanno said.
Analysts said the bolsa was strictly conditioned by Wall Street, which in turn showed high volatility on speculation surrounding the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy on interest rates.

"There's no local news moving the market these days," said an analyst at a leading local bank. "The focus is entirely on the second stage of (Fed chairman Alan) Greenspan's congressional testimony tomorrow and (U.S.) jobs data Friday."
Technical analysts said if the markets cleared the hurdles of Greenspan's speech and the jobs report, the MerVal could move towards a target of 735 next week.
Floor volume recovered to 32.2 million pesos from 24.6 million Monday, while over-the-counter volume picked up to 113.8 million from 86.6 million Monday.
The broad market index closed up 0.8 percent, with winners smashing losers 45 to 14 and 13 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier gainers were power generator Central Puerto and steelmaker Siderar, which surged 5.9 percent and 5.4 percent each. Heaviest losers were holding company Comercial del Plata, pulp maker Celulosa and real estate developer Irsa, off 2.5 percent, 2.1 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively.
